openai.feedback:
- Category: spec
- Severity: high
- File: .shipwright/planning/campaigns/2026-07-23-req3-ac-evidence-ledger-mono.md:1169
- Finding: The change marks “recorded exactly once, even from simultaneous producers” fully enforced while explicitly exempting `triage_add.py`. Two concurrent invocations of that CLI can still use the non-deduplicating append path and create duplicates; redefining “producers” to exclude that caller is not supported by the criterion.
- Suggestion: Route `triage_add.py` through an idempotent/deduplicating path, or retain an explicit unresolved status and follow-up for the manual-concurrency case.

- Category: spec
- Severity: high
- File: shared/scripts/lib/triage_plain_append_scope.py:139
- Finding: The proposed gate intentionally recognizes only `from triage ...` / `import triage`. A new automated producer can use standard package-qualified or relative imports, such as `from shared.scripts.triage import append_triage_item`, and call the plain append without appearing in the registry. This is a direct bypass of the mechanisable requirement the scanner is meant to enforce.
- Suggestion: Resolve the repository’s canonical qualified and relative import forms for `triage.py` (and test them as violations), rather than recording them as accepted gaps while claiming the criterion is closed.

Ship-with-fixes: the new guard catches the current convention, but it does not establish the claimed complete protection against future plain-append producers or concurrent manual calls.

SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: revise

glm.feedback:
I reviewed the scanner, the scope engine, and the test files against the spec ("no prompt-only/mechanisable line left unaddressed"). The core implementation is sound: the AST approach, scope-chain resolution, registry guard, and unparseable-file reporting all match what the ledger row's named oracle requires, and the ledger update itself is coherent. Findings:

- Category: edge-case
  Severity: low
  File: `shared/scripts/lib/triage_plain_append_scope.py` (~the `ImportFrom` non-target branch, `if alias.name != "*": bind_other(...)`)
  Finding: A star import from an unrelated module (`from other import *`) is not recorded as a binding at all, so it cannot shadow/conflict with a same-scope `from triage import append_triage_item`. If both appear at the same scope and `other` also exports `append_triage_item`, real Python makes the name ambiguous but the scanner flags it as a hit (false positive). Contrived, but it is the one binding shape that is silently skipped rather than recorded.
  Suggestion: Either document this in the accepted-gaps list, or record a wildcard binding marker in `other_names` for every name bound anywhere in the file so same-scope star imports become "ambiguous, do not flag".

- Category: bug
  Severity: low
  File: `shared/scripts/lib/triage_plain_append_scope.py` (`ast.Import` branch, `alias.name.split(".", 1)[0]`)
  Finding: `import triage.sub` (a dotted import whose first component is literally `triage`) is bound into `other_names` as `triage`, which would shadow a genuine same-scope `import triage` and un-flag a real violating call. Also `import other.triage` binds `other`, never the receiver name used in `other.triage.append_triage_item(...)` — but that shape is part of documented gap #1, so only the `triage.<something>` shadow is an unrecorded limit.
  Suggestion: Add it to the accepted-gaps list or check the full dotted name against `module_name` before falling back to the first component.

- Category: test
  Severity: low
  File: `shared/tests/test_triage_append_producer_registry.py` (`test_no_unparseable_file_is_a_silent_scan_gap` + `test_no_unregistered_module_calls_plain_append`)
  Finding: The two live-repo tests each walk and parse the entire repository independently (and `find_plain_append_callers` re-parses files `find_unparseable_files` already parsed). On a large tree this doubles an already repo-wide AST parse per test run. Not a correctness defect, but a real CI-cost regression worth a module-level cache or a shared fixture.
  Suggestion: Memoize `_parse` per path (e.g. `functools.lru_cache` keyed on resolved path string), or compute both results in one session-scoped fixture.

- Category: edge-case
  Severity: low
  File: `shared/scripts/lib/triage_plain_append_scan.py` (`EXCLUDED_PARTS`)
  Finding: Any directory named `tests` anywhere is excluded wholesale. The justification (CLAUDE.md plugin convention) is reasonable, but the exclusion is structural, not verified: a producer placed under a path containing a `tests/` component (e.g. a plugin shipping code in `tests/` contrary to convention, or a file like `plugins/x/tests/helpers/prod_writer.py`) evades the scan silently, with no `find_unparseable_files`-style surfacing. This is exactly the "silent evasion" shape the module exists to close, just one level removed.
  Suggestion: At minimum, note the directory-name exclusion as a named gap in the module docstring alongside limits 1–3, so it is auditable rather than implicit.

- Category: edge-case
  Severity: low
  File: `shared/scripts/lib/triage_plain_append_scan.py` (`_calls_plain_append`, star-import branch)
  Finding: `from triage import *` adds only `append_triage_item` to `plain_names`; it does not make `triage` available as an attribute receiver (correct Python semantics), but if the star-exported module ever also exports a same-named helper under an alias, there is no ambiguity handling — star imports are treated as unconditionally binding the target. Safe direction for this use, so this is informational only.

I found no correctness bugs that would make the registry test pass while the guarantee is broken: the reverse-guard tests exercise `_assert_registry_matches` itself (the round-9 fix is genuinely applied), the rogue-producer and different-top-level-directory tests use the default bases, and the unparseable-file pin is live. The ledger update correctly closes FR-01.14 #1's mechanisable half and re-accounts the remaining three prompt-only/mechanisable occurrences with explicit reasons.

Overall assessment: ship-as-is — the findings above are refinements and documentation of narrow, mostly-contrived limits, none of which undermine the guarantee the spec asks for.

SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: approve
